subject: Film & Cinema
title: Framing and Negative Space
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Framing and Negative Space.

hook.text: Sometimes what's empty in the frame matters more than what's filled.

buildup.text: Negative space — the empty area around a subject — creates isolation, vulnerability, or dread.

discovery.text: No Country for Old Men uses vast, empty landscapes to dwarf characters against an indifferent world.

twist.text: Cramped framing does the opposite — tight spaces create claustrophobia and pressure.

climax.text: The relationship between subject and space is one of cinema's most eloquent tools.

quiz.question: What does negative space in a film frame typically convey?
